rows.sum: Strong operating quarter with 33% revenue and 36% operating EBITDA growth on record ADR, PAT up 27% to Rs 95 cr despite higher JV losses, likely mildly positive for the stock if not already priced in.
A clean Q2 with 10.5% revenue and ~10% PAT growth, margin expansion and a 33% larger order book, though MHE weakness and filing during market hours temper the upside.

Canara Bank posted standalone profit up 8.4% YoY to Rs 5,175 crore on lower provisions and better asset quality, but weak other income and flat core operating profit make it an in-line, unexciting quarter.
Revenue grew 19% on the ACT acquisition, but flat EBITDA, compressed margins and a swing to a consolidated loss make this a weak quarter that is likely to weigh on the stock.

Revenue jumped 61% and headline consolidated profit of ~Rs 50 crore looks huge, but it is almost entirely a one-off deconsolidation gain, with core pre-exceptional profit down YoY and propped by other income and provision reversals.
Solid operating quarter with 15% YoY revenue growth and 70bps QoQ margin expansion despite wage hikes, but flat sequential PAT on lower other income and higher tax tempers the upside.
DEN's revenue keeps shrinking and core cable/broadband operations are losing more money, with the small profit rise driven wholly by treasury other income, so a muted to negative reaction is likely.
A clean, record quarter with 20% revenue growth and 50% PAT growth, helped by lower finance costs and a growing MTF book, which reads as a modestly positive result for a recently listed broker.

A strong, operations-driven Q2 with 61% revenue growth, margin recovery to about 16% and a big jump in order inflow, though flattered by a weak base quarter, which leaves a modest upside bias for the next session.
Strong YoY growth and a tripled order book on a low base, offset by a sharp QoQ drop in sales and profit and a CFO exit, so the first-session reaction is likely mixed.

PNB Gilts swung to a Rs 45 cr profit from a loss a year ago, but profit fell sharply from Q1 on a trading loss; the result is decent but not exciting for a volatile, rate-driven stock, and it was released mid-session.
YoY growth looks solid but the quarter breaks the recent improving trend with a sharp sequential margin and profit decline on absorbed cost inflation, so the stock could see mild selling.

Consolidated revenue fell 21% YoY and profit dropped ~79% as real estate income dried up; the sequential profit jump is largely a deferred tax credit, so the quarter reads weak despite growing product sales.

Core AMC operations are solid, with revenue up 16% YoY and operating profit up about 16%, but a collapse in treasury other income left headline PAT up only 6% YoY and down 8% QoQ, so the first-session reaction may be muted.
HCLTech posted a solid Q2 with a sharp margin recovery, record profit and strong bookings, though underlying CC growth stays low single digit, so expect a modestly positive reaction.

Headline profit nearly tripled with strong NII, margin and asset-quality gains, but EPS is flat after the Emirates NBD dilution and treasury gains flattered the quarter, so a modest positive reaction is likely.

This micro-cap with almost no operations swung to a Rs 30 lakh quarterly loss as sales fell back QoQ, carries an auditor qualification over large doubtful inter-corporate loans, and has negligible cash, so the result is poor.

A small microcap turned profitable on a 45% revenue jump led by exports, but the margin is thin and partly propped by other income; the filing came out during market hours, so a modest positive reaction is plausible.
Clean, record quarter with 26% revenue and 22% PAT growth on strong tractor engine volumes and steady margins, released mid-session, so modest upside is likely if it beats expectations.

Revenue was in line with the pre-announced update, but margin compression held consolidated PAT growth to about 8.5%, so the market may read it as a mild disappointment despite better like-for-like growth.
Strong ~39% revenue growth and record profit (+22.5% YoY) are offset by a third straight quarter of margin compression, making this a good but not clean beat for a small-cap.
Indbank Merchant Banking's Q2 revenue was flat at Rs 6.36 cr while cost growth and mark-to-market losses cut net profit 13% YoY and 32% QoQ, a soft quarter for a small-cap PSU broker.
Core fee revenue grew 17% YoY and PAT 21%, but profit fell sharply QoQ as treasury gains faded and SIP flows weakened, making this a decent but unexciting quarter.

Can Fin Homes posted a steady but unexciting Q2: profit is up about 10% YoY on 10% AUM growth, margins and asset quality are stable, and loan growth is soft, so the stock is unlikely to see a strong move either way.

Underlying business grew a steady ~22% with record inflows and on-track guidance, but reported PAT is down 11% on ESOP costs, so the reaction likely hinges on whether the market accepts the adjusted numbers.
A solid H1 with VNB up 24%, margin expansion and 17% premium growth, offset by lower solvency and a new sub-debt raise, so expect a modest positive to neutral reaction.
A clean beat-style quarter: profit up 22% QoQ, with falling credit costs, better asset quality and expanding RoA, though high expectations on this rerated NBFC may cap the upside.

TCS posted a steady quarter, with profit up 15% YoY on a low base, but constant-currency growth was a sluggish 0.5% QoQ and margins were slightly lower, a largely in-line result unlikely to move the stock much.
Insolvent RCOM's loss narrowed on one-off exceptional gains while revenue keeps shrinking and auditors heavily qualify the accounts, so the result carries little positive information for the stock.
TV Vision is now in insolvency (CIRP) with revenue almost gone and losses understated by unbooked interest and impairments, so the narrower loss is meaningless and equity holders face likely wipeout.
Profit doubled YoY off a tiny base, but margins and profit collapsed versus the strong March quarter and debt rose, so the market is likely to read this as a disappointing QoQ reversal.

Jinkushal's Q1 consolidated profit collapsed 66% YoY to Rs 2.2 cr despite 16% revenue growth, as freight, staff costs and a heavy overseas inventory build squeezed margins to roughly 5%, a weak print for a small recently listed stock.

Revenue surged and the company swung back to a small profit, but near-zero margins and active ED, SFIO and SEBI investigations keep the stock's risk profile dominated by regulatory overhang rather than the numbers.
A defunct, zero-revenue textile group posted another ~Rs 51 cr consolidated loss with insolvency proceedings pending and interest unprovided, so there is nothing positive here for a distressed stock.
Deep consolidated loss of Rs 87 crore on large impairments and write-offs, with a qualified review, going-concern doubt and an ongoing debt default, reads very poorly despite flat toll revenue.

Headline profit is small and down sharply YoY, the remaining business after the mall sale is loss-making, and the Nagpur NOC overhang persists, so this is a weak read with the Inorbit deal the only support.

EPS of about Rs 59 versus about Rs 33 a year ago points to a strong roughly 80% profit jump that extends the March-quarter surge, partly clouded by a wholesale leadership reshuffle and an unreadable results table.
Monsoon-quarter revenue grew modestly but profit fell about 41% on fuel- and maintenance-driven cost inflation, partly offset by the announcement of a room-expansion plan.

Aksh Optifibre's Q1 numbers are not visible in the filing text, and the company is under CIRP with an NCLAT stay pending, so insolvency risk rather than earnings will drive the stock and the bias is negative.
Vinny Overseas grew sales 32% YoY to Rs 33.6 cr, but net profit fell 27% to Rs 0.21 cr on razor-thin margins and reliance on other income, making this a weak quarter for a penny-stock.
Standalone loss narrowed to Rs 14.8 crore on 22% revenue growth in a seasonally weak quarter, but an adverse auditor conclusion and going-concern doubts keep quality very poor.

Revenue grew only 4.8% and profit collapsed about 70% YoY on input-cost pressure from legacy orders; record orders and a 33% larger backlog soften the blow, but margin erosion over two straight quarters likely weighs on the stock.
Small-cap aluminium extruder posts 33% revenue growth and 60% profit growth YoY to a record Rs 3.8 cr quarter, though sales dipped sequentially and interest costs rose sharply.

Headline profit tripled only because of an unexplained Rs 20 cr other-income gain, while the operating segments slipped into a loss and revenue fell YoY; a Rs 500 cr fund-raise plan adds dilution risk.
Q1 FY27 profit rose 32% YoY to Rs 4.7 cr on flat-ish revenue, but halved sequentially from a strong March quarter and leans on other income, so the read is decent but not exciting.

Revenue more than doubled YoY, but consolidated PAT fell 26% YoY and about 80% QoQ on a sharp sequential revenue drop, manufacturing losses and heavy reliance on other income, so the stock likely reacts negatively.
REPL swung back to a small profit after a heavy Q4 loss, but revenue halved YoY and profit fell ~78%, leaving underlying business weak.
Rubicon posted a strong Q1 with consolidated revenue up 52% and profit up 96% YoY, partly aided by the Arinna acquisition, continuing a sharp growth trend that should be received positively.

Only the auditor reports came through, so the quarter cannot be scored; an unreviewed Rs 0.49 crore associate profit may flatter consolidated earnings, and the outlook stays neutral near the base rate.
R&B Denims grew revenue 16% YoY but consolidated profit nearly halved on weak margins, a modest sequential recovery from a poor March quarter that likely disappoints.
Modi Rubber's Q1 profit of Rs 4.25 cr (down 13% YoY) is carried entirely by JV share and other income while core operations remain loss-making, a muted result for an illiquid stock.
Rishabh posted modest 4% consolidated revenue growth with flat net profit as a weaker Europe and a normalised tax rate offset strong India growth, a mixed print unlikely to excite.
Tiny Ahmedabad realty firm posted a wider Q1 net loss of about Rs 0.2 crore on Rs 2.1 crore revenue, a seasonally weak quarter with no positive catalyst.
Priti International's Q1 revenue fell 52% YoY to Rs 3.4 cr with the solar trading business gone and profit down 54%, entirely carried by other income, a weak print for an illiquid microcap.
Micro-cap Libas posted a thin Rs 0.05 cr consolidated profit on a 30% revenue drop, with garments loss-making and only rock salt holding up, plus governance sloppiness—weak underlying read.
Emmbi posted ~11% YoY consolidated revenue growth and a ~54% jump in net profit to Rs 2.3 cr with no one-offs, a clean beat on its recent trend, though it was slightly softer sequentially.

Lux posted a flat Q1 with revenue up under 1% and profit roughly unchanged, as Vertical A gains were offset by weakness in Vertical B and higher interest costs, so this is a lacklustre print unlikely to excite the stock.
Rudra posted modest 7% revenue growth but a 7% YoY dip in net profit to Rs 3.6 cr, a QoQ recovery but no clear improvement in thin margins, so likely a muted reaction.

Kitex posted a fourth straight consolidated loss (Rs 17 cr), with revenue down about 20% YoY and a repeat auditor qualification, while announcing a Rs 3,000 cr QIP that raises dilution worries, so the bias is negative for the stock.
YoY turnaround with solid pre-sales and collections, but a steep QoQ fall in revenue and profit, tax-aided PAT and a slow start against aggressive guidance make this a mixed print.
The microcap posted strong consolidated revenue growth (+48% YoY) and roughly doubled PBT, driven by its non-BFSI business, but the illegible filing and thin margins limit conviction.
Q1 revenue slipped about 5% YoY and a tax true-up wiped out profit to near zero, extending a weak trend for this small industrial-fibres company.
Revenue collapsed 41% YoY and nearly 60% QoQ, leaving profit dependent on other income, a weak print likely to pressure this illiquid small-cap.

Standalone profit jump rests on lumpy other income, offset by a Rs 10.85 cr healthcare impairment, board resignations and weak debt coverage, and the consolidated picture likely remains loss-making, so the read is weak.
Revenue grew 20% but margins compressed again and attributable PAT fell ~19% YoY to Rs 2.9 cr, with management warning of further cost pressure, a likely negative read despite large order wins.

IZMO's Q1 consolidated profit doubled YoY to Rs 12.2 cr on 16% revenue growth and better margins, but nil tax provision, unreviewed foreign-subsidiary numbers and a steep QoQ drop from a lumpy March quarter temper the read.

The filing as extracted contains only the board outcome and audit reports, with no headline numbers, so the read is neutral with a seasonally soft Q1 expected; the base rate applies with a slight negative tilt.

Tarmat's Q1 revenue appears to be up about 44% YoY, but profit looks flat-to-lower on EPS around 0.23, and recurring auditor concerns over an unconsolidated JV cloud the picture, making this a mixed result for a small illiquid stock.

Profit jumped about six-fold YoY to ~Rs 25 cr on a textile margin recovery despite an ~19% sales drop, but heavy other income tempers the quality, making this a modestly positive read for a small-cap.
A very weak quarter, with consolidated profit down about 95% YoY on a 43% revenue drop, partly cushioned by a buyback being evaluated, which may limit the downside.
Pilani's Q1 swung to a deeper Rs 47 cr consolidated loss as interest income fell ~71% while finance costs rose, though large OCI investment gains boosted book value for this illiquid holding company.
Ajooni's sales doubled but profit nearly halved on wafer-thin margins and rising debt, a weak print for a low-priced microcap likely to drift lower.
Clean quarter: revenue +12% and profit +67% YoY on better margins with no forex or one-off support, though profit was below a flattered Q4, so a modestly positive reaction is likely.

Manaksia posted strong headline growth with consolidated PAT up ~73% YoY to Rs 26.7 cr on 28% revenue growth, though heavy other income and unallocable gains temper the quality.
