Omaxe posted a surprise consolidated swing to a marginal Rs 1.3 cr profit on 44% revenue growth, with a lower interest burden, but that profit rests on other income and the standalone business is still loss-making, so expect a modestly positive reaction.

A recently listed stainless maker posted a record quarter, with revenue up ~31% and PAT up ~80% YoY, helped by lower interest after IPO debt paydown; that reads clearly positive, though some of the growth is low-margin trading.
Tiny revenue base shrank sharply and the small profit is carried by other income and by skipping depreciation, while an undisclosed slump sale adds uncertainty; this reads as weak.
Strong 36% revenue growth but margins sharply compressed and net profit nearly halved YoY to Rs 6.2 cr, with more debt planned — a weak quarter.
Q1 revenue jumped 51% YoY and net profit rose 22% to Rs 5.1 crore with a sharp sequential margin recovery, a solid but not spectacular print for a small-cap cotton ginner.

Weak Q1: consolidated revenue fell 33% YoY and net profit fell 53% to Rs 1.52 cr, the second-lowest quarter in the recent trend, with surging depreciation; this illiquid DVR stock is more likely to drift lower than rise.

Valiant Organics posted a sharp earnings jump with 13% revenue growth, best-in-years operating margin (~17% EBITDA standalone) and pharma turnaround, partly aided by associate income, making it a clearly strong quarter.
Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell 33% YoY to Rs 4.5 cr and net profit halved to Rs 1.52 cr as depreciation surged, a weak print for a penny stock.
Flat sales and a near-breakeven core business; the Rs 11 cr profit rests on Rs 14 cr of treasury/MTM other income, so earnings quality is poor despite the rebound from a Q4 loss.

Wabag posted 21% revenue and 37% PAT growth with a record Rs194 bn order book, though profit growth is flattered by a forex gain swing and gross margins narrowed, making the beat less clean than the headline suggests.

Solid ~18% YoY revenue growth, but consolidated PAT grew only ~13% to Rs 64.9 crore and fell sequentially as raw material and staff costs squeezed margins, so this reads as a decent but unexciting quarter.

Jagran's Q1 shows healthy ad-led revenue growth and a radio turnaround, but core print margins compressed on raw material costs and reported PAT fell 8% YoY, leaving a mixed print with governance overhang.
Revenue jumped 74% YoY but the Rs 6.9 cr profit is entirely a one-off land/leasehold gain, with core margins collapsing from the March quarter, so the headline turnaround is weak in quality.

Seasonally small Q1 shows profit up sharply from a low base on 28% revenue growth, but the numbers carry no tax provision and an auditor qualification, and an illiquid small cap may see a muted reaction.

Astral posted strong Q1 profit growth of ~52% on a weak base with plumbing margin expansion despite flat volumes and a weak industry, a solid but partly expected beat that should lean mildly positive.
Cotton yarn maker SRTL appears to show strong revenue growth but only about 5% net profit growth, alongside a change in how IPO funds are used, which reads as a mixed quarter with limited upside.
HINDCON posted a strong June quarter: revenue up about 43% YoY, profit up about 70%+, and margins recovered sharply to around 15%, with no exceptional items and a clean limited review.
Headline profit of Rs 41 cr is a one-off land-sale gain masking a 19% revenue drop and a core business that is barely breaking even, so the print is weak underneath.

Consolidated revenue more than doubled and PAT rose 73% on the Netcom acquisition, with a 2x FY27 revenue target, though margins compressed and interest costs surged, making this a good but largely inorganic quarter.

Solid volume-led 19-23% revenue growth and good cash flow, but margins compressed and the headline 83% consolidated profit jump is largely a Tata Capital MTM gain, so the core read is good rather than spectacular.

Revenue jumped 42% YoY and attributable profit rose to Rs 25.8 cr from Rs 15.8 cr, but about half of pre-tax profit comes from an unrealised mutual fund mark-to-market gain, so the core improvement is real but more modest than the headline.
Q1 profit edged up 6% YoY on better distillery margins despite a 24% revenue fall, but the June fire that shut the 200 KLPD ethanol plant clouds Q2 and the result is mixed.

Lenskart posted a strong Q1: revenue up 43% (34% like-for-like), PAT nearly quadrupled to Rs 228 cr and the international business turned solidly profitable, a clear beat on trend though valuation may cap the reaction.

Standalone swung to Rs 17.6 cr profit only on a Rs 28 cr exceptional write-back, while core is loss-making with no operating revenue, a qualified review and the auditor resigning, though debt repayment and IBC withdrawal ease liquidity fears.

A weak Q1: revenue fell a third and profit nearly halved, hit by war-related freight disruption and lower pass-through realisations, with management guiding to continued low mango realisations, so the stock likely trades down.

OnMobile posted a Rs 289 Mn consolidated Q1 loss as revenue slipped about 2% YoY, other income vanished and restructuring costs hit, leaving the core barely EBITDA-positive despite the ONMO+ launch, a weak read for the stock.

The filing text shows only a clean review report and a tiny solar SPV investment, not the June quarter numbers, so the stock's reaction depends on figures not visible here; treat this as roughly a base-rate call.

Q1 shows shrinking revenue on both standalone and consolidated bases and compressed EPC margins, with only flat standalone profit, a thin order book and a delayed SPV sale, which makes this a weak print likely to weigh on the stock.
Strong 21% top-line growth and tariff parity commentary, but flat margins, rising interest/depreciation and other-income-heavy PBT keep profit growth modest at 7% YoY.
SEPC grew revenue 35% YoY but swung to a Rs 11 cr net loss on a DTA write-off, with weaker underlying PBT and continued auditor qualifications, a negative read for the stock.
The filing text shows only board outcomes (new CFO, re-appointments) and no Q1 numbers, and against a weak margin trend the default lean is slightly negative.

Big YoY jump off a tiny base but consolidated PAT of ~Rs 9.6 cr and an 8% OPM are well below the Q3-Q4 run-rate, with the new Chemdist segment loss-making, so the quarter reads as mixed despite the strong order book.
A sharp margin-led profit collapse (PAT -76% YoY) on flat sales outweighs management's promise of Q2 recovery and refinancing benefits, so expect selling pressure.

The core casino business keeps shrinking YoY, but the reported ₹212 cr loss is driven by a GST provision far smaller than the feared ₹16,800 cr demand, which likely makes the reaction mixed rather than sharply negative.

Indo Tech's Q1 FY27 standalone numbers are not readable in this filing, so with only a dividend, an ESOP plan and higher borrowing limits to go on, the reaction is close to a coin flip with a slight downside lean.

AYM Syntex swung to a Rs 8.7 cr profit from a year-ago loss, with margins near 9% sustaining the Q4 recovery, though about a quarter of the profit is a one-off tax credit and the result softened sequentially.
Q1 consolidated profit rose ~17% YoY on just ~2% revenue growth, helped by higher other income and offset by Brazil subsidiary losses, a middling print for a recently listed stock.
Revenue grew ~52% YoY, but net profit was flat at Rs 4.65 cr and fell sharply QoQ, with margins squeezed and a Rs 80 lakh GST hit, so the stock is likely neutral to soft.

Headline profit tripled YoY on 4% revenue growth and a sharp margin expansion, but the auditor's disclaimer over inventory valuation, which directly drives the margin, makes the numbers unreliable; expect a muted to negative reaction in an illiquid small cap.
The board approved Q1 FY27 results, but the extract shows no numbers, so the read defaults to a base-rate, neutral view on a thin-margin, illiquid small cap.
Price-led revenue growth of 67% failed to translate into profit: margins compressed sharply below guidance and PAT slipped 3% YoY, so a muted-to-negative reaction is likely.

Filing text lacks the actual Q1 numbers and mostly covers fund-utilisation and governance items, including a commingling flag, so with margins trending down the bias is slightly negative pending the figures.

Clean, strong Q1 with consolidated PAT more than doubling on margin expansion and reaffirmed Rs 5,000 cr FY27 guidance, though revenue dipped QoQ and the guidance implies a steep ramp-up later in the year.
Profit nearly doubled YoY on a thin ~3% net margin despite flat sales, but a large unprovided GST demand of about Rs 43 cr hangs over this small, illiquid aluminium stock.
Solid Q1 with record revenue, ~14% sales and ~24% PAT growth and better margins led by aligners, though lab segment profit weakness and slower adjusted EBITDA growth temper the beat.

Polyplex posted a sharp consolidated turnaround, with revenue up ~30% YoY and owners' profit of Rs 91 cr against a loss a year ago, well above recent quarters, though the standalone business softened and minority interest takes a big share.
Revenue grew ~20% YoY but consolidated profit fell (−16% on continuing ops, −31% headline) on lower other income and thin EPC margins, a disappointing print versus the recent trend.

Faze Three's Q1 revenue grew 8% YoY, but margin compression, a loss-making US subsidiary and higher interest costs cut consolidated profit 25% to Rs 9.6 cr, with other income propping up PBT, so this reads as a weak quarter.
PI Industries posted a 10% YoY revenue decline and 39% PAT drop with margins well below last year and pharma losses widening, though it improved sequentially from a weak March quarter.
Aries Agro posted a clean Q1 with ~16% revenue growth and ~50% consolidated profit growth on better margins, no one-offs, a modestly positive read for a small-cap.

Bata's Q1 shows modest ~4% sales growth but better margins, a 23% PAT rise (helped partly by last year's VRS charge) and a large Rs 25 interim dividend, a decent print likely to be received mildly positively.

EPACK grew Q1 revenue 34% but consolidated profit nearly halved on thin margins, rising interest and JV losses, with a continuing audit qualification on a disputed receivable—an underwhelming peak-season print.

Simplex posted ~20% YoY revenue growth and roughly doubled profit to Rs 10.7 cr on a clean basis, but profit fell sharply from the March quarter, margins remain thin and debt overhang lingers, so expect a muted reaction.
Starteck Finance posted a solid Q1 with consolidated revenue up ~39% and PAT up ~22% YoY on better core lending income, though profit dipped versus Q4 and the stock is a thinly traded small-cap.
Operations were solid, with 14.5% revenue and 37% EBITDA growth, but consolidated profit fell 30% on higher depreciation, interest and tax; the Adani Ports hire as MD may cushion the reaction.
Solid Q1 with 26% revenue and 30% profit growth to record levels, though part of the profit lift came from higher other income while core margins were roughly flat.
Syncom posted a strong Q1 with consolidated PAT up ~58% YoY on just 7% sales growth thanks to sharp margin expansion, though inventory build and other income temper quality.
Revenue collapsed about 64% YoY to Rs 18.3 crore and the thin reported profit is clouded by extensive repeat audit qualifications and an NSE compliance fine, a weak setup for this microcap.
Mufti's Q1 FY27 was weak: revenue grew only 4%, while higher marketing spend cut EBITDA margin by 460 bps and net profit fell 63% to Rs2.3 cr, much of it propped up by other income.
Revenue jumped 49% on acquisitions, but margins compressed sharply and attributable profit actually declined YoY, so this reads as a mixed quarter with mild downside risk.
Dish TV's Q1 consolidated revenue fell 19% YoY and losses tripled to Rs 286 cr with DTH bleeding and going-concern doubts, a clearly poor result for a penny stock in structural decline.
Q1 revenue collapsed 63% YoY to Rs 107 cr on few handovers, with flat profit of Rs 13 cr propped by other income, though rising customer advances and land buying support the longer-term pipeline.
Linde India grew revenue 22% YoY but margins compressed and consolidated profit slipped 2% to Rs 105 cr, with a continued auditor qualification and SEBI overhang, making this a mixed print.
A strong, clean Q1 with 34% revenue and 42% PAT growth and stable margins, though the disclosure of errors needing restatement of FY26 accounts may temper the reaction.

Headline profit more than doubled YoY but leans heavily on other income and fell sequentially in revenue, while a same-day auditor resignation and odd replacement auditor raise governance concerns likely to weigh on the stock.

Q1 revenue grew 9.5% but profit roughly halved on segment losses in hygiene and beverages, margin compression and a lease-rent exceptional charge, a weak print versus the improving trend of recent quarters.

Revenue doubled on low-margin trading, but profit collapsed 95% YoY against an other-income-boosted base, and the pharma unit is loss-making during its plant upgrade, so this is a weak print for a micro-cap.
Q1 FY27 consolidated sales fell 31% YoY and profit nearly vanished as the Bhopal plant licence issue crippled the standalone business, leaving only a token profit after last quarter's loss.
Losses narrowed YoY on 41% revenue growth, but the company remains loss-making, the train-control business has no revenue, and the auditor flagged financial stress, so the read is weak.
Flair grew Q1 revenue ~11% but margin squeeze from raw materials and lower other income left consolidated PAT flat YoY and down 20% QoQ, a soft print likely to weigh on the stock.
Flat revenue with a wider Rs 11.8 cr loss, negative net worth and a going-concern uncertainty flag make this a poor quarter for the stock despite management's turnaround talk.
Q1 profit nearly tripled YoY to Rs 158 cr on 34% revenue growth, but about half of pre-tax profit came from an unexplained surge in other income, though core operations still improved clearly.

Revenue nearly doubled YoY and the company stayed in profit for a third straight quarter, but the thin profit rests on other income and fell QoQ as Heavy Engineering margins compressed, so the reaction looks balanced.

TARC posted its first clean operating profit in a while, with revenue of Rs 217 cr and PAT of Rs 22.6 cr on Tripundra recognition plus strong presales, but PAT is down YoY against a tax-aided base and earnings remain lumpy, making this a mixed print.
Landmark Cars posted a solid Q1 with revenue up ~23% and net profit roughly doubling YoY on better margins, though profit was flat sequentially versus the March quarter.

GTL's Rs 322 cr profit is pure OTS accounting gain; the core business swung to a loss with an auditor-modified review, so the stock's reaction hinges on debt-resolution sentiment rather than earnings.
Q1 standalone PAT ₹114 cr (+5.7% YoY), helped by a lower tax rate; consolidated PAT ₹121.6 cr (+5.6%); loan growth stays sub-10% and credit costs are rising, so this is a lukewarm quarter.
Filing text lacks the actual Q1 numbers; with a strong recent trend but no visible data and no dividend, expect a roughly base-rate reaction.

Strong 44% revenue growth and a swing to a small consolidated profit point to an operational turnaround, but the profit relies on a one-off lease gain, so the result is good on trend rather than clean.
Divgi posted a blowout Q1 with revenue nearly doubling and profit almost tripling YoY on clean operating gains and margin expansion, well above the recent run-rate.
Tiny metals firm doubled profit YoY on 61% sales growth, but the quarter fell well short of the strong March quarter on both revenue and margins, so the reaction is likely muted to mildly negative.
Bafna's Q1 was very weak: sales down 23% YoY, core operations swung to a loss and the tiny Rs 0.08 cr profit came only from other income, with an unprovided GST dispute also flagged by the auditor.

AKI's consolidated sales rose 64% YoY and profit doubled off a tiny base, but revenue fell sharply QoQ, standalone profit declined, and earnings rest on other income, so the stock is likely to see little sustained upside.
Suyog's Q1 consolidated PAT fell 16% YoY to Rs 14.5 crore on 6% revenue growth as finance and depreciation costs rose, with accrued unbilled revenue and control caveats weighing on quality.

A clean quarter: consolidated revenue rose 24% and PAT 35% YoY on volume, pricing and margin gains plus lower interest, with the Saudi JV loss as a small drag, making this a good but not spectacular print for a recent IPO.
Post-merger Gujarat Energy posted a strong Q1 with consolidated PAT nearly doubling YoY to Rs 1,007 cr on a gas-trading windfall, though restated comparatives and trading volatility temper the read.

Tiny real-estate firm posts a sharp YoY jump in revenue and profit to Rs38 lakh with its first positive operating margin in a while, but the scale is minuscule and other income still props up earnings.
A solid Q1 with ~18% revenue growth and 33% profit growth YoY, though rising interest costs, an inventory build and sizable other income temper it for a small-cap.
Shilchar's Q1 shows revenue down 15% and profit down 50% YoY with margins collapsing to around 16%, a clear deterioration likely to pressure the stock.
Orient Press slipped back into a wider loss (Rs 1.25 cr) on an 18% revenue drop with flexible packaging bleeding, undoing the recovery of the last two quarters.

Steel trader Shiv Aum posted about 25% YoY revenue growth and roughly 2.5x net profit at Rs 3.8 cr, though the quarter was softer than March, and its planned BSE main-board listing is a mild positive.

Om Infra swung to a Rs6.5 cr consolidated profit on 19% revenue growth versus a loss a year ago, but it fell sharply from March, the audit review is qualified, and a large OCI hit on investments clouds the picture.

Max India's revenue grew 63% YoY but fell QoQ, and the consolidated loss nearly doubled sequentially to Rs 36 cr as senior living swung to a loss and lease-surrender costs rose, reversing the improvement seen in Q4.
Tiny shell-like financier swings back to a Rs 0.93 cr profit, but it is down about a third YoY and carried entirely by other income and investment gains, so it is a weak, low-quality print.
Strong quarter with 57% revenue growth and profit more than tripling YoY (up 26% QoQ) with improving NPAs, though rising credit costs and leverage temper the read.
Strong revenue growth and a return to profit after a loss-hit Q4, but margins and PAT fell YoY on gas costs and trading mix, making this a mixed print for a low-margin small-cap.
TD Power posted a clean, strong Q1 with revenue and PAT both up about 72% YoY to record levels and stable-to-better operating margins, which should support the stock despite high expectations.

Headline profit is inflated by about Rs 144 cr of one-off other income, likely from the MR Organisation divestment, while core operations show 40% YoY revenue growth but a sharp margin squeeze and a sequential dip.
Weak quarter, with revenue down about 6% YoY and halved QoQ, profit roughly halved to about Rs 0.5 crore, heavy audit qualifications and a promoter stake sale, so a negative bias.

Q1 revenue appears to have nearly tripled to about Rs 303 crore and PBT rose sequentially to about Rs 12 crore, but margins stay thin and the garbled filing leaves net profit unconfirmed, so this is a cautiously positive but uncertain read.

Sales grew ~30% YoY but pre-tax profit collapsed to near zero, with the reported Rs 1.09 cr profit coming almost entirely from a deferred tax credit, so the headline flatters a weak operating quarter.

Headline profit halved YoY only because last year's quarter had a large other-income boost; underlying operating performance improved and QoQ it is a clear rebound from a loss, but the stock is thin and the result is modest.
Flat revenue but a solid margin-led profit rebound (PAT +20% YoY, +34% QoQ) plus a 1:5 split announcement makes this a modestly positive print.
Q1 FY27 numbers are not visible in this filing extract, so it reads as neutral beyond the internally funded Unit 4 loom expansion, with the reaction depending on figures not shown here.
BSL is back in profit at Rs 1.7 cr, with 7% revenue growth and margins at 8.5%, a decent rebound for a small, heavily leveraged textile maker that could draw mild buying.
Profit jumped to Rs 2.3 cr, but it comes almost entirely from other income on the property-sale cash while the core rental business is flat, so there is little new information for the stock.

The filing covers only the board outcome and a director reappointment, with no Q1 FY27 numbers in the text, and the company's recent trend of thin, shrinking margins gives little reason to expect a positive reaction in an illiquid small-cap.
Q1 revenue fell 8% YoY and profit dropped a third to Rs 19 cr, with a new fraud disclosure and auditor emphasis of matter likely to weigh on the stock despite modest pre-sales growth.
RBZ Jewellers posted strong 60% YoY revenue growth and 28% profit growth in Q1, though margins narrowed and interest costs rose, a solid but not spectacular print for a small-cap.

Q1 consolidated revenue rose 18% and PAT 16% to ~21 cr on strong branded alcobev growth, but margins compressed on higher depreciation and staff costs, leaving an in-line seasonal quarter that rests on ambitious H2 guidance.
Revenue grew 26% on low-margin hardware, but core services profit and net profit fell about a third YoY with margins compressing, a weak quarter for this small-cap IT name.
The board outcome is filed but the Q1 numbers are not visible; the recent trend shows growing sales with margins stuck near 11-12%, so the setup is neutral pending the actual figures.
EPL posted record 25% revenue growth and raised guidance, but margins slipped and PAT was flat on a higher tax rate, leaving a mixed read likely to see a muted reaction.

Manappuram posted a record Q1 consolidated profit of Rs585 cr (+343% YoY, +44% QoQ) on doubling gold loan AUM even after a Rs125 cr extra provision, a clearly strong print tempered by microfinance subsidiary compliance issues and margin compression.

Underlying volume and comparable revenue growth are strong and a stock split is announced, but consolidated profit fell 12% with margins squeezed by raw material inflation, and the headline standalone PAT jump is a subsidiary dividend.
Flat-to-slightly-weaker June quarter for this low-margin edible oil processor: revenue grew 8% but consolidated profit slipped 6% YoY, though it rebounded sharply from a soft March quarter.

A solid quarter with 22% revenue growth, sharp margin expansion and 55% profit growth, but revenue dipped sequentially, FY27 guidance looks stretched and dilution tempers EPS growth, so the first-day move is likely close to a coin flip.

A clean quarter with a sharp margin-led profit jump (PAT +83%, EBITDA margin 14.5%) on modest 6% revenue growth reads positively after a write-down-hit March quarter, though weak top-line growth may cap the reaction.
TBZ posted strong YoY growth (revenue +35%, PAT +51%) in a tough quarter, but margins fell well short of the elevated Q3/Q4 FY26 levels, so the reaction is likely modestly positive at best.

Sunflag's Q1 FY27 consolidated profit of Rs 66 cr is up ~6% YoY on 6.5% revenue growth with flat margins, a steady but unexciting quarter whose big comprehensive income comes from the Lloyds Metals stake MTM rather than operations.

Rubfila's Q1 shows an ~8% YoY revenue decline and ~13% lower consolidated profit, with an auditor qualification over an unsupported contingency provision, a weak quarter for a small-cap likely to drift lower.

Consolidated profit more than halved YoY to Rs 8.4 cr on a 3.7% revenue decline, and operating margins collapsed to about 4%, with earnings propped up by other income and a customer-compensation exceptional item; standalone sales growth is the only bright spot.
Alembic's Q1 consolidated PAT rose 5% to Rs 65 cr purely on its Alembic Pharma stake, while its own real estate and API operations weakened, a mixed result likely tracking the associate's stock.
Headline profit of Rs 7.5 cr is entirely a one-off land-sale gain; core operations swung to a Rs 2.9 cr loss on 19% lower revenue, a weak underlying quarter.

IFCI's Q1 consolidated profit held near last year's level at ~Rs 60 cr only thanks to provision write-backs and other income, while revenue fell 20% and the parent remains capital-negative with ~96% gross NPAs, a weak print for a sentiment-driven stock.
Revenue grew 17% YoY, but profit was flat and fell 72% sequentially, with the entire pre-tax profit coming from other income, a weak print for this microcap after a strong March quarter.

Camlin grew revenue 27% YoY on acquisitions, but operating EBITDA shrank and the consolidated loss widened to about Rs 32 crore, extending a run of loss-making quarters with no sign of a margin turnaround.
Q1 FY27 sales fell 40% YoY and profit halved to Rs 0.6 cr with inventory piling up, a weak print for this small-cap belt maker.

TNPETRO's first quarter after its expansion shutdown shows revenue up 68% and profit more than doubling with clearly better margins, a strong print likely to be bought, though filed just after market close so it trades tomorrow.

This investment-holding NBFC swung to a ₹1.1 cr Q1 profit from a year-ago loss on higher dividend income, but the earnings are lumpy, the stock is illiquid, and the chairman has died, so expect little directional signal.
Veedol posted a record consolidated quarter: revenue rose 18% and PAT 57% YoY on a sharp margin expansion led by overseas subsidiaries, though the domestic standalone business was soft.

Revenue recovered and losses narrowed, but the company remains loss-making with a going-concern warning, negative net worth and promoters barred by SEBI, so the improvement is unlikely to excite buyers.
Revenue grew 24% but consolidated profit halved, with core construction operations loss-making and the bottom line held up only by other income and a liability write-back.

Revathi's seasonally weak Q1 improved: consolidated revenue rose 35% YoY and profit climbed to Rs 2.0 cr from Rs 0.6 cr, but other income and unreviewed subsidiary numbers do much of the work, so the stock's reaction may be muted.
Mazda posted a strong Q1 with revenue up 62% and net profit up about 49% YoY to roughly Rs 7.3 cr on broad-based segment growth, though other income remains a meaningful part of profit.
Strong 34% YoY revenue and 26% PAT growth, but profit fell 11% sequentially on margin compression, making it a mixed read for a richly valued growth stock.

A clean record quarter with PAT up 86% YoY and 22% QoQ, driven by better per-ton profitability and mix, plus a capacity ramp and a new OEM deal, which should support a positive reaction for this recently listed stock.
Breakout quarter with consolidated revenue up ~2.5x YoY and PAT of Rs 21 cr versus under Rs 2 cr in prior quarters, driven by a subsidiary ramp-up and not by one-offs, which should spark buying.
Revenue flat and PAT down 11% YoY as rising depreciation and weak cash logistics offset better EBITDA margins and order wins, leaving a mixed quarter for a stock in an earnings downtrend.

Manaksia Steels posted a record quarter with PAT more than tripling YoY on ~51% revenue growth and margins holding near 11%, plus an Rs 800 cr expansion plan, which should be read positively for this small-cap.
Q1 revenue of Rs 68.6 cr is a big jump YoY but a steep sequential drop with a return to small loss and sharply lower gross margin, so the stock may struggle despite order book and QIP comfort.

Headline 60% revenue and 116% PAT growth are mostly due to acquisitions and a low fire-hit base, while margins compressed, standalone profit fell, and profit slipped QoQ; this reads as a mixed result.
Q1 revenue fell 9% and PAT halved YoY with rising debt and thin order inflow, partly offset by a sequential margin uptick and an asset-sale announcement, so expect mild pressure.

Revenue grew 17% to Rs 2,229 Cr, but EBITDA fell 11% and PAT fell 45% to Rs 56 Cr as margins dropped to 11.9%, with CDMO and Generics segment profits collapsing and an FDA warning letter at Montreal, so expect pressure despite guidance for an H2 recovery.

Strong YoY quarter with 31% revenue growth, margin expansion and a near-doubled order book, though sequentially flat with Middle East subsidiary weakness, so a modestly positive reaction is more likely than not.
Strong YoY growth on a low base, but revenue and profit fell sharply from a blockbuster Q4 with margins contracting, so the quarter reads as a sequential disappointment for a momentum stock.
Ind-Swift Labs posted a sharp operating turnaround with ~21% revenue growth and nearly tripled profit on much higher margins, a clearly strong quarter for a small-cap likely to see buying interest.

Vi delivered its best operating quarter in a while, with 3.2% QoQ revenue growth, its first net subscriber add and ARPU of Rs 195, but the headline loss is cushioned by a Rs 1,816 Cr share-remeasurement gain, so expect a mildly positive reaction.

Strong top-line growth and a sharp GFS margin recovery lift underlying PAT ~156%, though reported PAT falls on a high one-off base and ISCS margins slipped sequentially, making this a good but not flawless quarter.
Solid 16% revenue growth and a 29% jump in PAT, but PBT was flat YoY and the beat rests on a lower tax rate, so expect only a modestly positive reaction.
Q1 FY27 numbers aren't visible in the filing text, but continued losses and ongoing capital support to the loss-making Dubai subsidiary point to a weak backdrop, so a downside bias is likely.
Solid Q1 with 17% revenue growth and 39% PAT growth on better operating profit despite lower other income, a modestly positive read for the stock.

Lloyds Metals posted a record quarter: consolidated PAT of Rs 1,734 cr is up 13% QoQ and standalone margins expanded on the steel ramp-up, though YoY growth is flattered by consolidation and leverage is rising.
Jaipur Kurti grew sales about 25% YoY, but rising interest and staff costs left net profit 6% lower at Rs 0.68 cr, a mixed print for a thinly-traded microcap.
Lotus Eye posted a 26% revenue jump and a return to profit with sharply better operating margins, though rising depreciation and interest from expansion temper net profit growth to about 13%.
A solid quarter: standalone revenue rose about 16% and PAT about 39% YoY on improving margins, extending the company's margin uptrend, though a low tax rate helps the bottom line.

A huge headline profit comes almost entirely from a one-off debt-settlement gain while the core textile business stays flat with ~2% margins, so the reaction depends on whether traders chase the headline EPS.

ITDC's Q1 shows flat revenue (+2.6%) and slightly lower net profit (Rs 9.9 cr vs Rs 10.2 cr) as higher tax and a weak travel division offset hotel strength, with heavy reliance on other income and persistent audit concerns.

Strong 70% revenue growth and the debt and pledge clean-up are positives, but the sharp margin compression and the sequential drop in revenue and profit make this a mixed print that may disappoint a momentum stock.

KEC's Q1 shows flat revenue, a 120bp margin squeeze and a 42% profit fall with standalone profit nearly wiped out, a clear miss that management blames on transitory factors, so the stock likely faces selling.
Sales jumped 34% YoY, but material-cost-driven margin compression to ~10% kept core profit growth to single digits and reported net profit fell 13% on a one-off-boosted base, so this reads as mixed.

Bosch posted strong 22% revenue growth and roughly 12% growth in core PBT; the headline PAT decline is purely a base-quarter exceptional effect, so this is a solid but not spectacular print for a richly valued stock.
Consolidated profit roughly doubled YoY to Rs65.9 cr on a strong treasury quarter (plus a ~Rs5 cr ESOP reversal), rebounding from a Q4 loss, though core fee and lending businesses softened.
Revenue fell ~10% YoY but consolidated profit jumped on subsidiary earnings, other income and a tax credit, so the headline profit growth is low quality for this illiquid penny stock.
Revenue grew 19% but margins fell about 780bp and PAT dropped 21% YoY, with soft domestic orders; H2 recovery guidance may limit but likely not offset negative reaction.

Core operating profit nearly tripled YoY with almost no other income and deleveraging is nearly done, but revenue dipped QoQ, part of the gain comes from a new mining subsidiary, dilution is heavy and the long-standing audit qualifications remain, so expect a modest positive bias.
Q1 FY27 consolidated profit fell over 90% YoY to about Rs 1.2 crore on flat-to-lower revenue as sugar margins vanished, a clearly weak print likely to pressure the stock.
Profit halved YoY to Rs 7 cr and the core business is still loss-making before other income; the polyester turnaround and the THREE ICC launch are positives, but the headline is weak.
Record revenue with 34.5% growth, but sharp margin compression left PAT flat YoY and well down QoQ, so the strong topline is unlikely to be rewarded.
Solid 23% revenue growth and sequential margin recovery, but headline 32% PAT growth is padded by a tax write-back, with underlying PBT up just ~5% YoY.
HLE Glascoat's Q1 consolidated profit fell over 80% YoY to a near-breakeven Rs 2 crore as the heat transfer business collapsed and costs surged, marking the weakest quarter in its recent trend.
Rupa posted a decent seasonally weak Q1 with consolidated revenue up 10% and net profit up ~50% on a low base, though margins remain thin and absolute profit is small.

Q1 FY27 shows revenue down ~6% YoY and consolidated profit down ~15% amid rising interest and depreciation costs, with a continuing auditor qualification over the fire-insurance receivable, pointing to a soft reaction.
Ddev Plastiks posted a record Q1 with revenue up 29% and profit up 22% YoY as new capacity kicked in, with no one-offs, but margins thinned slightly and interest costs rose.
S Chand posted double-digit Q1 revenue growth, but cost inflation and the absence of a tax credit widened its seasonal net loss to Rs 18.7 cr, a modestly disappointing print.

Antony Waste's Q1 profit nearly vanished (Rs 0.75 crore vs Rs 23 crore YoY) on flat-to-lower revenue, higher costs and interest, with a damaging Pune plant accident and landfill litigation still pending, so expect selling.
A record completion-driven quarter (income Rs 937 cr, PAT Rs 146 cr) after several loss quarters, plus a big Mumbai project pipeline, should read positively even though pre-sales were flat.
A solid YoY quarter with a record Rs 9.2 cr PAT and 18% revenue growth, but revenue dipped sequentially and margin fell from Q4's 30%, so the reaction will likely be muted for this small-cap.

Fusion's recovery continues with Rs 62 cr PBT, falling credit costs and better NPA and margins, though AUM growth is flat and tax-free profit flatters PAT, making this a solid but partly expected turnaround print.
The filing pairs an unreadable Q1 FY27 P&L with a Rs 150 crore dilutive CCD issue and a capacity upgrade, so the setup is neutral to slightly cautious pending the actual numbers.
Dollar's Q1 profit rose 22% on better margins from price hikes, but flat 1.4% revenue growth and an inventory build temper the read, making for a mixed reaction.
Revenue jumped on mark-to-market gains but costs rose faster, leaving consolidated profit of Rs 0.86 cr down 14% YoY though well up QoQ, a mixed small-cap print.
Small steel maker posts flat-ish quarter with sales down 3% YoY but profit up 7% to Rs 3.96 cr on slightly better margins, unlikely to move the stock much.

GFL swung to a Rs 7.4 cr consolidated profit from a year-ago loss on PVR INOX's associate share, but profit fell steeply from March, and as a holding company the stock tracks PVR INOX more than its own numbers.

Strong YoY quarter with 33% revenue growth, an 83% PAT jump and margin expansion plus a new M&M-backed capex, though it is flat-to-down QoQ and partly reflects an easy base, so the upside reaction is likely modest.

The micro-cap marble firm swung to a cleaner operating profit, with PAT of Rs 0.82 cr vs Rs 0.60 cr a year ago on revenue up more than 4x, though the gain is largely trading revenue and inventory-driven, so the reaction is likely muted to modestly positive.

Gland posted a solid Q1 with 20% revenue growth and 47% PAT growth YoY on margin expansion, though profit fell 14% from a strong Q4, so the reaction likely hinges on whether the market focuses on YoY or QoQ.
Q1 consolidated PAT was flat YoY at Rs 45 cr: strong fee growth offset a collapse in treasury gains, with a lower tax rate helping, so the result reads as mixed and stalls the growth trend.
The tripling of headline profit is a one-off deferred-tax write-back. Underlying PBT fell about 65% on flat revenue and thinner margins, so expect limited upside once traders look past the EPS.
Revenue grew 14% but a raw-material squeeze cut EBITDA margin to 11.5% and profit fell 39%, a sharp miss against a steady ~19-20% margin history; recovery guidance may only soften the selling.

A record quarter with consolidated revenue up 21% and PAT up 61% YoY on better realisations and exports, plus new capacity now running, makes this a strong print for the small-cap, though part of the gain looks tied to rising crude prices.
Jaro's seasonally weak Q1 showed solid 17% revenue growth and 48% PAT growth, helped partly by IPO-cash other income and lower interest, a decent but not spectacular print.
A sharp miss: consolidated revenue fell 8% YoY and net profit 43% as margins collapsed to about 15%, extending the deterioration seen in recent quarters and likely to trigger heavy selling.
Strong YoY recovery with revenue up 33% and profit about 4.6x, but a sequential dip in sales, margin and profit from a tax-aided March quarter makes this a decent rather than standout print.
Roto's Q1 shows 15% revenue growth and a 47% profit jump flattered by a low-tax base, with margins stabilising after a declining trend—a decent beat versus recent weak quarters.
Profit grew a solid 18.5% YoY on better margins, but revenue slipped sequentially and growth slowed to under 7%, so this reads as an in-line-to-soft quarter for a richly valued stock.
Salzer grew sales 13% but material-cost pressure cut operating margin to about 6% and halved net profit YoY, extending a deteriorating margin trend, which is likely to weigh on the stock.
Q1 consolidated revenue rose 14.5% on strong tractor sales, but flat cranes and higher depreciation held PAT growth to about 4% at Rs 5.7 cr, a lukewarm print.

Coal trader Anmol India posted Q1 profit of Rs 6.0 cr, slightly above last year and well above the March quarter, but revenue fell 21% YoY and other income props up thin trading margins, so this reads as a mixed result.
A clean, strong Q1: revenue up 20% and profit up 42% YoY, with operating margins near 17% and a sharp recovery from a weak March quarter, though the result is still below the late-2025 peak.
Revenue grew 31% YoY but Windsor slipped to an operating pre-tax loss on higher interest and corporate costs, a weak print against a profitable prior quarter.

Revenue growth resumed (+19% YoY) and the cash arbitration award plus fresh order wins help sentiment, but underlying profit of ~Rs156 cr after stripping the one-off is only moderately better than the recent trend, so a modest positive reaction is likely rather than a strong one.

Banco's Q1 FY27 numbers can't be read from the filing; the auditor gave a clean review and the trend after a strong March quarter is neutral, so treat it as a coin-flip near the base rate until the actual figures are seen.
Small textile maker posted flat sales but net profit up ~62% YoY to Rs 2.35 cr on better operating margins, a modest positive for an illiquid micro-cap.

Strong rebound quarter with revenue up 15% and profit up 64% YoY, though a large chunk of the profit jump came from treasury gains, so the core textile improvement is solid but less dramatic than the headline.
Affle delivered a clean, in-line ~20% revenue and ~22% PAT growth quarter with flat margins, solid but likely largely expected, with a Bobble insolvency overhang.
Flat revenue but net profit down 44% YoY to Rs 18 crore as EBITDA margin slid to about 11% from 17%, a weak start to the year that is likely to weigh on the stock.
Strong 33% topline growth and 41% PAT growth in Q1, but margins are flat YoY and down sequentially, so the reaction should be modestly positive rather than euphoric.

HBL's Q1 shows modest 6% revenue growth but a 24% YoY profit decline with defence batteries collapsing and electronics margins well below last year's peak, likely disappointing a market priced for the Kavach-led ramp.
Strong 48% revenue growth and the best profit in five quarters for this small textile firm, though margins are thin and profit benefits from nil tax provisioning.
Strong YoY volume and revenue growth off a weak base, but margins and profit fell sharply versus the strong Dec/Mar quarters, so the market may read it as a sequential disappointment.

Delhivery's Q1 revenue grew 28% YoY on the Ecom acquisition but margins slumped to ~5% and profit fell 65% YoY to Rs 32 cr, propped up by other income, alongside COO Ajith Pai's exit — a disappointing print likely to pressure the stock.
Double-digit topline growth but flat EBITDA and a wider pre-tax loss show expansion is still burning profitability, so the stock is likely to trade soft.

Sales slipped about 9% YoY, but sharply lower interest cost lifted net profit 66% to Rs 3.6 cr. That reads as decent deleveraging-led earnings for a thinly traded small-cap, with a near coin-flip open.

Headline 88% revenue growth is mostly acquired, while margins compressed sharply and profit fell 31% QoQ, with a going-concern emphasis on subsidiaries, so the result reads as mixed for a richly valued defence stock.
Akums posted a clean beat on its own trend, with 14% revenue growth, about 240 bp EBITDA margin expansion and PAT up 56% YoY led by CDMO, though a Rs156 cr tax demand overhang remains.
TVS Electronics swung back to a wider Q1 loss of Rs 6.6 cr despite ~10% revenue growth, as margins collapsed in both segments, breaking the recent recovery trend.

Record revenue and a 61% YoY profit jump, though much of the profit gain comes from goodwill amortisation ending while operating margins stayed flat near 7%, making this a solid but not spectacular quarter.
Beardsell grew Q1 revenue 10% but margins collapsed on higher material costs, PBT fell a third YoY and PAT down 22% only thanks to a deferred tax credit, a weak print for a small-cap.

The micro-cap turnaround shell posted record revenue of Rs 8.5 cr and a clean Rs 4.3 cr profit against losses a year ago and last quarter, a strong print on paper, but trading is likely to be volatile and illiquid.

Record quarter with 57% revenue growth, steady ~10% margins, consolidated PAT doubling and a large optical-fibre JV expansion should be received well, tempered by rising interest costs and a CFO exit.
Strong 44% YoY revenue growth, but EBITDA margin fell to 16% and PAT nearly halved QoQ with meaningful other-income support, so the 57% YoY headline overstates quality.

A clean, strong consolidated quarter with net profit nearly doubling YoY to Rs 20.8 cr (the best in several quarters) on a hydraulics turnaround and aerospace growth, partly offset by weaker standalone profit.
Q1 profit rose ~23% on a sharp cable margin recovery and associate income, but revenue fell 21% as EPC stalled on Jal Jeevan fund delays and rising debt costs, making this a mixed print.
Strong YoY growth with revenue more than doubling and profit up ~60%, but a sharp sequential drop in profit and thinner margins temper the read for this small-cap textile maker.
Q1 consolidated revenue rose 9% and PAT 19% on lower interest costs, but EBITDA grew only ~7% with slight margin compression, a steady but unexciting quarter.
Q1 growth is solid at ~27% revenue and PAT, but the core DG margin compressed and management explicitly guided a subdued H1 on input-cost pressure, which may weigh on the recently listed stock.
Onida grew Q1 sales ~30% YoY but still lost Rs 14 cr with a deeper operating loss, so the turnaround remains unproven.
Strong Q1 with revenue up ~39% and PAT up ~65% YoY on improved margins, partly helped by forex gain and JV profit, plus a fresh capex for CDMO capacity—likely viewed positively.
Revenue was flat and PAT fell 9% YoY as consumerware and furniture shrank and margins contracted, leaving only writing instruments growing, a weak quarter likely to pressure the stock.

A sharp sequential recovery to near break-even (loss Rs 0.55 cr vs Rs 33.6 cr in Q4) on revenue that tripled QoQ, but the near break-even leans on other income and an inventory build, amid continued equity dilution in a penny stock.
Bharat Wire Ropes posted a third straight soft quarter, with revenue down 8% YoY to Rs 130 cr, net profit down 22% to Rs 12.2 cr and margins compressing, so expect a negative reaction.
Subros grew revenue 17.5% YoY but margin compression kept net profit flat at ~Rs 41.5 cr, and the EV compressor tie-up is a long-dated positive that likely won't offset the weak operating leverage.

Q1 shows solid YoY growth off a weak base, with revenue up 15%, PAT up 43%, better margins, a strong order book and sharply lower debt, though absolute profit stays thin and seasonally low, making this a modestly positive read.
Revenue grew 19% but consolidated PAT slipped about 5% YoY to Rs 108 cr on margin compression and weaker per-tonne bauxite economics, a middling quarter that is unlikely to excite the stock.

Strong year-on-year growth flattered by a low base (last year's exceptional item) and bullion sales, with profit down sequentially and margins slightly thinner, so expect a modestly positive but uncertain reaction.

Flat-ish Q1 for the Jindal holding company with profit up 3% on an unchanged annual dividend, and a large OCI mark-to-market gain that the market already sees in underlying share prices, so little catalyst.
Strong 25% revenue growth and stable ~28% EBITDA margin, but a higher tax rate and depreciation cap PAT growth at 11%, making this a solid but not spectacular quarter.
A small-base profit jump on lower interest costs and a record order book are offset by falling revenue, flat EBITDA and thin margins, making this an unconvincing quarter for the stock.

Tiny, legally troubled preschool operator posted a 20% YoY revenue drop and a Rs 2.1 cr loss driven by large other expenses, with recovery of key deposits looking doubtful—negative read for an illiquid microcap.
Strong pre-sales and revenue growth, but profit fell YoY and collapsed QoQ as interest costs surged, leaving a soft headline that may weigh on the stock despite reiterated guidance.
Revenue grew 40% but consolidated PAT fell 24% YoY on margin compression, higher depreciation and interest, and a high tax rate, so the stock is likely to see pressure given its premium valuation.

Record quarter with consolidated PAT nearly doubling on high crude realisation, 11% production growth and a windfall refining margin at NRL; strong, though the market may treat part of it as price-driven and already expected.
Defunct textile shell posted a wider Rs 1.3 cr loss on near-zero revenue, and adverse Supreme Court rulings on ~Rs 20 cr electricity dues remain unprovided, a clear negative overhang.

HGS posted a wider Q1 consolidated loss of Rs 66 cr on flat revenue of Rs 1,050 cr, with BPM margins weakening and Media losses deepening, and it is still kept afloat by other income, a clearly weak print.

Gloster swung to a Rs 8.2 cr consolidated profit on 40% revenue growth, with the cables loss fixed and jute steady, but profit was flat versus the March quarter, so this is a decent but not a breakout print.
A seasonally tiny Q1 for this core investment company, with a small loss and revenue down 86% YoY, matters little next to the Rs 137 crore OCI portfolio gain, so expect a muted reaction.

The filing text has no figures, and given the shell-like trend of near-zero sales and operating losses against a one-off-heavy June 2025 base, expect a weak year-on-year comparison with little else to move the stock.
Volume grew 12% but falling prices and fuel/packing cost spikes cut EBITDA 22% and core pre-tax profit ~75%, leaving net profit down 63% at Rs31 cr, a clear miss on margins.
Solid YoY profit jump on a weak base with margins near 10%, but flat-to-lower sequential revenue and adjusted margin make it a decent but unexciting quarter.
Loss-making Praxis gave no readable Q1 numbers, while announcing an open-ended equity fund raise and a bigger ESOP pool, so dilution worries outweigh any comfort from fresh capital.

Arvee posted record Q1 revenue of Rs 17.2 cr (+130% YoY) and profit of Rs 1.69 cr versus Rs 0.17 cr, a strong but lumpy SME result, offset slightly by the unexplained postponement of its scheme of arrangement.
Strong acquisition-led quarter with consolidated profit up 72% YoY and a sequential gain in owner EPS, though large minority interests and rising interest costs temper the headline.
CARE Ratings posted a solid Q1 with ~19% revenue and ~25% profit growth YoY and better operating margins, a clean beat on its weak year-ago base though seasonally soft versus March.
Revenue grew 8% YoY, but consolidated profit fell 29% YoY on a JV loss and weaker margins versus last year, though the quarter was a modest sequential improvement, so the read is mixed to soft.

Q1 FY27 numbers are unreadable in this filing, though the subsidiary's Rs 3.11 crore profit hints at a decent quarter; without the headline figures the outlook is roughly neutral against a strong FY26 base.
Clean quarter with 31% revenue growth and margin recovery off a fire-hit base, but sequential margin and pre-exceptional profit softened, so reaction is likely modestly positive to flat.

A breakout quarter: consolidated PAT rises to about Rs 27.5 cr from Rs 1.6 cr on 14% revenue growth and a sharp margin expansion in textiles, which is likely to spark buying in this small-cap despite questions over sustainability.
Small profit rise to Rs 8.4 cr is driven by investment and other income while real estate revenue collapsed 62%, with the ICD arbitration dispute still overhanging—a mixed, low-quality quarter.

Q1 is a clear YoY turnaround with 18% revenue growth, a return to profit and chipboard turning EBITDA positive, but it is a seasonal step down from a strong Q4, so the read is good rather than a surprise.

Strong ~50% revenue growth and a swing back to small profit versus the prior quarter's loss, but profit still relies on other income and treasury gains while the healthcare business keeps losing money.

Afcons swung back to a thin Rs30 cr profit but revenue fell 21% and PAT 78% YoY with profit essentially carried by other income; the strong Rs13,219 cr order inflow is the main offset, so expect a muted-to-negative reaction.
Headline PAT nearly doubled to Rs 52.7 cr, but about half is a mark-to-market investment gain; underlying operations still improved solidly, with 23% revenue growth and core margins back near 27%.

GPIL posted record revenue up 32% YoY, but margins fell sharply to about 19% and net profit was nearly flat YoY and down 21% QoQ, so the top-line growth is likely to be overshadowed by the margin squeeze.

Ravinder Heights reported a wider Q1 consolidated loss of Rs 1.69 cr on near-zero operating revenue, with nothing new beyond last year's one-off deposit income, so expect a muted to slightly negative reaction.
Q1 is a clean beat on profitability, with PAT up 17% on just 4% revenue growth as margins expanded, though weak AI and flat domestic branded sales temper it; mildly positive for the stock.
Headline PAT up 16% YoY but revenue fell 5% and over half of pre-tax profit came from treasury/other income, so core pipe business is only modestly better YoY and weaker sequentially.
Revenue jumped 40% YoY, but net profit fell 15% and EPS dropped by a third due to lower other income, weaker JV share, thinner margins and dilution, a mixed print.

Revenue grew a solid 30% YoY, but rising staff and amortisation costs pushed IRIS into a consolidated net loss and revenue fell sharply from Q4, so expect a negative reaction despite upbeat ARR commentary.
A strong Q1: revenue +69% and PAT more than doubled YoY with margins near 16% and a record backlog, though profit dipped QoQ and expectations for this richly valued stock are high.
Revenue grew a solid 26% YoY, but PBT fell about 24% sequentially and net profit was flat-to-down QoQ, helped by a low tax charge, which reads as a soft quarter for a richly valued growth stock.
Q1 profit of ~Rs27 cr, up roughly 13x YoY and slightly above Q4, confirms the margin recovery on modestly higher sales, a solid but partly expected print.

Solid YoY growth in continuing engineering operations with better auto-component margins, but revenue is flat QoQ, segment profit dipped sequentially and other income is a large share of profit, so the likely reaction is modestly positive to neutral.

Q1 profit fell over 80% YoY as sugar segment margins vanished on costly inventory, with PBT entirely covered by other income, though firmer July sugar prices and deferred volumes offer some recovery hope.

Univastu more than tripled revenue YoY and grew PAT about 2.5x, holding the step-up in scale from Q4, though at thinner ~13% margins and with stretched receivables; a strong YoY print for a small-cap that should lean positive.
Orient Paper's loss narrowed to Rs 8.3 cr on modest paper-segment improvement but revenue slipped 4.5% and the business remains loss-making, a mixed print unlikely to re-rate the stock.

Sequential volume and revenue recovery is real, but YoY revenue is down 45%, and about Rs81 cr of the loss reduction comes from a provision write-back the auditor qualified plus an amortisation change, so the headline improvement overstates progress.
Inox Wind's Q1 consolidated PAT fell about a third YoY to Rs 64 cr with flat EBITDA, heavy reliance on other income and recurring audit emphasis matters, a soft print likely to weigh on the stock.
Revenue and PBT grew on new Ghatampur capacity, but headline consolidated PAT nearly halved YoY and fell sharply QoQ on a normal tax charge, which likely reads negative at the open.
Headline consolidated PAT up 54% YoY but it's driven by higher other income and a low base, while revenue grew just 4% and core segment profit fell, so a flat-to-soft reaction is likely.
Eastern Silk appears to have posted another loss-making quarter on tiny, stagnant sales with persistently negative margins, giving little reason for a rally.
Modest single-digit YoY growth with margins well below the last two quarters' 16-17% and rising interest/depreciation makes this a lukewarm Q1 against strong recent momentum.

Pokarna's Q1 consolidated profit jumped ~51% YoY to Rs 42.6 cr on 11% revenue growth, with OPM recovering to ~33% and lower interest costs, a clear rebound from a weak FY26 that should be received positively.
Titan posted 40% ex-bullion income growth and 63% PAT growth, but ~Rs 407 cr of duty gains flatter it; adjusted ~37% PBT growth is still solid, likely mildly positive reception.

Bigbloc grew Q1 revenue 40% YoY and cut losses sharply, but remains loss-making at the consolidated level with a sequential revenue dip and a recurring Ind AS 19 qualification, making this a mixed, near-breakeven print.

Headline profit nearly doubled, but it came almost entirely from other income while O&M revenue fell about 17% YoY to a multi-quarter low, with recurring auditor emphasis items, so the quality reads weak.

Record quarter with 18% consolidated revenue growth and a sharp margin expansion to ~25% OPM, driving net profit up 18% (about 26% on core PBT) despite lower other income — a clear beat on recent trend.
Q1 FY27 profit fell 40% YoY on weaker sugar margins and lower sales, only partly offset by a better distillery and lower interest costs, so expect mild selling pressure.

Q1 revenue was flat YoY, operating margin halved, and the small consolidated profit rests on other income and a tax credit while the standalone business posted a loss, so this reads as weak for the stock.

Only the board-meeting outcome letter is visible, with no Q1 numbers, so for a loss-making micro-cap spinner that was just turning operationally positive, the first-session odds stay near the base rate.
NCL's Q1 FY27 outcome letter confirms the results and a Rs 2 dividend but the extract gives no numbers, so the stock likely trades on the actual figures with no clear edge.

Revenue grew YoY, but margins collapsed QoQ and the company swung to a Rs 46 cr consolidated loss after a settlement charge, so the quarter reads as a clear miss against the recent margin-expansion trend.
Q1 grew modestly year on year (revenue +12%, PAT +21%) but fell sharply from a strong Q4 with margins down, which may disappoint a richly valued CRDMO stock.

IRM Energy posted a record Q1 with revenue up 24% and profit up about 143% on a sharp per-unit margin jump, though management hints the margin boost is partly temporary and related-party receivable issues persist.
Strong 35% revenue growth but margins compressed ~120bp and profit growth leaned on a doubling of other income, so a largely pre-known volume beat may get a muted reaction.

Lupin delivered strong Q1 operating growth (sales +33%, PBT +42.5%), with the US and international markets leading, but a normalised tax rate held PAT growth to 16% and PAT dipped QoQ, so the reaction is likely positive but modest.

Strong 35% revenue growth to a record Rs 2,034 cr with a 14% PAT rise and improved core earnings, though margins remain compressed by commodities — a recovery quarter likely to be received modestly positively.
Vikram Solar posted strong 38% revenue growth but profit crashed ~85% YoY to about Rs 20 crore on a sharp collapse in module margins, a clear negative surprise likely to pressure the stock.
Rain posted a record quarter, with revenue up 17% YoY and net profit roughly quadrupling to Rs 341 cr on sharply better margins, well above the recent trend, though debt and inventory rose.
Strong Q1 with 23% revenue growth, record margins and 38% PAT growth driven by volumes, which should support the stock despite rising interest costs and a rich valuation.
IFB posted strong 18% revenue growth and ~65% profit growth on better home appliance margins with no one-offs, a solid quarter though margins remain modest.

Operations were modestly better, with profit up 45% YoY on lower interest costs, but the insolvency petition against the parent, the qualified review report and multiple agency probes dominate, so a muted to negative reaction is likely.

The tiny trading-led company swung to a continuing-ops profit with 89% revenue growth, but net profit fell YoY, sales slipped QoQ and going-concern doubts persist pending the Reid & Taylor demerger, so this reads as a mixed quarter.
Q1 sales were flat at about Rs 229 cr and net profit fell roughly 27% YoY to about Rs 7.3 cr, extending the margin-erosion trend despite a rebound from a weak March quarter.
SCI posted a record Q1 with revenue up 40% and profit up 75% YoY on a tanker windfall and bulk turnaround, partly offset by JV losses, so the setup is positive for the stock.

Solid Q1 with 16.6% revenue growth and margin expansion driving PBT up 85%, though other income is a large chunk of profit and management flags raw-material cost pressure ahead, making this good but not a blowout.
Revenue grew ~10% but costs swamped it, with consolidated PBT down 39% and PAT down 21% YoY as the core India business margin weakened, a disappointing quarter extending the margin slide.
Q1 standalone revenue grew 21% but margins slipped and lower other income kept profit flat YoY, while a bigger Rs 250 cr QIP offsets the stock-split cheer, so expect a mixed reaction.

T T Ltd's board outcome leaves the Q1 numbers unseen in the text and highlights lapsed preferential warrants as investors declined to pay the balance, a mild negative for a small, thin-margin textile company.

Fortis delivered strong 17.5% topline growth but margins slipped and profit grew only 2% as acquisitions and ESOP costs weighed, making this a mixed quarter likely to disappoint a richly valued stock.

HCG posted solid Q1 with 13% revenue and 20% adjusted EBITDA growth and owner PAT nearly tripling off a low base, though profitability remains thin and partly flattered by a divestment gain and adjusted metrics.
Q1 sales grew ~8% but net profit nearly halved to Rs 9 cr as cement margins compressed and paints losses widened, a weak print versus last year's Rs 16.9 cr.
A clear recovery quarter for this small-cap logistics player, with revenue up 31% and profit up 40% YoY after a weak Q4, though margins are still razor-thin.
Strong recovery quarter with PAT up 12x YoY and 14% QoQ, improving asset quality and a rating upgrade, though part of the QoQ lift came from higher assignment fair-value gains.

Revenue grew a healthy ~15% but costs ate the gain, leaving underlying consolidated profit flat YoY (headline +226% only due to last year's exceptional write-down), a lukewarm read for a richly valued hotel stock.
Britannia posted clean Q1 with 9.5% sales growth and 14% profit growth with YoY margin expansion despite cost headwinds, plus upbeat exit-rate commentary, a modestly positive read for the stock.
Q1 standalone revenue fell 10.5% and net profit fell 20.5% YoY as plantation earnings weakened, with nearly half of pre-tax profit coming from other income; a soft result for this illiquid tea stock.
Solid 19% revenue and PBT growth led by international services, but net profit fell 14% YoY on a normalised tax rate and government/solutions business shrank, making this a mixed quarter.

Linc's Q1 FY27 was weak: revenue was flat, polymer costs compressed margins and attributable profit fell about 18% YoY, with management guiding for more near-term cost pressure, so the stock is likely to see mild selling.
Flat revenue and a sharp headline profit drop (on a high exceptional-laden base) make Q1 underwhelming, though the Prestige stake deal provides some support.

Lumpy investment-income-driven quarter roughly doubled YoY profit to Rs 7.5 cr including a small exceptional gain, but fell far below the March quarter, leaving a mixed-to-positive read for this illiquid stock.

Orient Ceratech's continuing business nearly tripled pre-tax profit YoY on modest 5% sales growth, with headline PAT doubling to Rs8.6cr despite a one-off loss on the power division sale, a decent but small-cap result.
Strong 28% sales growth and ~49% profit growth in the key summer quarter, but margins remain thin at ~4%, making this a decent but not stellar recovery print.
Headline Q1 profit up ~28% on ~19% revenue growth, but operating margin fell to around 15% from 18% and treasury gains carried much of the profit growth, so the read is mixed.
Sundrop posted a solid Q1 with 15% consolidated revenue growth and nearly tripled PAT to Rs 12.1 cr, continuing its margin recovery, though margins remain thin and the base was weak.

Underlying coffee operations improved, with revenue up about 8% and a positive operating result, but headline profit collapsed to near zero without one-off gains, and the auditor's disclaimer keeps the sentiment risk tilted down.
Clean quarter with 11% revenue growth and margins back to ~20%, reversing a two-quarter slowdown; profit up 8.5% YoY and 34% QoQ, mildly positive for the stock.

Cosmo First posted strong 46% YoY revenue growth and a 25% PAT rise to a record Rs 54 cr with better core profitability, though margins thinned and standalone profit was flat, making for a good but not spectacular quarter.

Solid YoY quarter with consolidated profit up 36% on steel strength and lower interest, but mining softened sequentially and the forest-lease afforestation demand overhangs, making a modestly positive reaction the likelier outcome.
Revenue grew 10% but reported 8% PAT growth rests on a one-off customs write-back; core operating profit and margins fell YoY and QoQ, a weak quality quarter.
Headline profit jump is a base effect; underlying margins compressed sharply on raw material costs, Europe nearly broke even, and the CFO resigned, so the result reads weak.
Record quarter with profit up ~4x YoY and 43% QoQ on ethanol margin expansion, but a Rs250cr QIP proposal may temper the reaction.
A shell-like business with shrinking revenue and a sharply wider Rs 16.7 cr loss under going-concern doubt, with tax refund and SC win offering only modest cash relief.

Operationally strong quarter with record revenue and sharply better GCM margins, but headline PAT growth is muted by vanished other income and standalone margin squeeze, leaving a modestly positive setup.
Sula's Q1 was weak: revenue grew only 2%, EBITDA fell 9% on grape costs, and the tiny Rs 1.06 cr profit was entirely propped up by a one-off property sale gain.
LIC posted a strong Q1 with VNB up 61% and margin at 22.9% plus 23% PAT growth, which should be read positively despite modest premium growth and post-OFS supply.

Solid quarter with 35% revenue and 50% profit growth, though partly helped by a low-depreciation base and an acquisition; flat solar profit sequentially and a proposed Rs 5,000 cr QIP may cap the reaction.
Revenue grew a healthy 13% but margins compressed sharply and consolidated profit fell 17% YoY, well below trend, so expect a negative reaction.
Decent YoY growth of about 20% in sales and 25% in profit, but a steep sequential fall from a strong March quarter, plus rising staff and depreciation costs, make this an unexciting result.
NCC posted a decent Q1 with 12% consolidated revenue and profit growth and better EBITDA margin, but flat standalone profit, rising interest costs and weak order inflow make it a middling print.

A clean quarter with no exceptional items: revenue rose 13% YoY and profit 48% on sharply better margins, though both dipped from the strong March quarter, so this reads as a solid YoY beat for a small-cap rice exporter.

IVP posted a record Q1 with profit up roughly 11x YoY on 12% sales growth, and the Rs137 cr port demand was quashed, though the margin is partly helped by an inventory build and there was a brief plant closure scare.

A loss-making quarter with sharply lower recognised revenue and thinner margins, partly offset by strong pre-sales and higher realisations from the Lamborghini-branded launch; with the pre-sales figure likely already known, a muted to slightly negative reaction is likely.

A sharply worse quarter: the consolidated loss widened to Rs 176 cr as both segments swung to losses, the March-quarter recovery reversed, and a post-quarter plant fire adds risk, so expect selling pressure.
